statuses.title: Return conservative privacy guarantees from Monte Carlo amplification
statuses.note: Re-derived from first principles, every inequality direction checked. samples_to_pmf (balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:271-390): per-rank Chernoff bound P[F(X_(j)) < p] <= exp(-n KL(j/n||p)) is the standard binomial bound, inverted on the conservative side (kl_lower_cdf_bound bisection returns the lower endpoint, :392-410); per-rank failure = mc_failure_probability/(2n) union-bounds n ranks x 2 adjacency directions; sample values bucketed by ceil (loss rounded up); constructed CDF <= true CDF at every point whp => stochastic domination => reported delta/epsilon are valid 1-beta upper bounds; residual 1-p_n goes to infinity_mass and is fail-closed checked against mc_resolution (:374-381); non-finite samples now error instead of being silently dropped (:282-295); total-mass conservation asserted (:383-388). resolved_num_mc_samples (discretization/config.rs:150-183) matches the last-rank residual 1-(failure/(2n))^(1/n) exactly. Guarantee threading: epsilon_at returns +inf when delta <= worst-case infinity mass (pld/mod.rs:288-293); beta_at/risk_at fail closed to 0 for MC PLDs; compose() adds failure probabilities (union bound) and combines resolutions as 1-(1-a)(1-b); self_compose keeps the single failure probability - sound because the one domination event implies domination of the k-fold composition. KL band verified below the exact Beta-inverse order-statistic bound by test (monte_carlo.rs:489-510); identity-Gram MC bound verified above the exact deterministic oracle (:645-671). b_min_sep MC (mc.rs) routes both directions through the same samples_to_pmf with num_directions=2. Cholesky covariance guarded by a residual check that errors rather than sampling the wrong covariance (:173-188). Metadata surfaces to Python (python/pld.rs mc_resolution/estimation_failure_probability) and pld() accepts mc_resolution/mc_failure_probability/seed (#573).

statuses.title: Apply learning-rate schedules on the MF step axis and expose weighted Grams
statuses.note: Commit 0baaba7a (#529): band-MF now applies lr as per-row query_weights in the optimizer objective (_band_mf.py:80-89 passes query_weights=lr to optimize_toeplitz; _toeplitz.per_query_error:536-547 multiplies per-row error by weight^2) instead of the old wrong-axis Toeplitz-coefficient product. lambda-CGD/BISR/BLT expose weighted Grams via native *_gram_matrix_lr with the schedule materialized on the step axis (materialize_schedule evaluates schedule(step) for each step, _schedule_fingerprint.py:12-18). statuses.title: Reuse column-keyed Gaussian draws across MF noise steps

statuses.title: Apply the full BISR strategy operator at runtime
statuses.note: Commit 2507548b (#509): BisrStrategy.streaming_matrix now computes strategy coefficients at the full horizon (native bisr_strategy_coefficients(inv, n_steps), _bisr.py:198-211) instead of the pre-fix bandwidth-truncated coefficients, and raw_noise_factory routes through the streaming engine with the horizon guard. Verified numerically at n=12, p=3: materialized runtime operator equals the exact banded-Toeplitz C^{-1} (normalized and unnormalized, max err 0.0), and row norms match. Caveat (reported as a finding): the runtime applies C^{-1} by forward-substitution against the DENSE length-n strategy coefficients, so the streaming state holds n_steps-1 gradient-sized buffers (measured: 2.04 GB and 4.27 s/step at n_steps=512, d=1e6) while docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/bisr.md:10,96,109 claim 'p-1 noise vectors (via PRNG replay)'.

statuses.title: Compute MF row norms without eager quadratic work

statuses.title: Define privacy accounting for loss-scaler skipped steps

statuses.title: Preserve clipping numerics across microbatching and bfloat16
statuses.note: Three layers verified in the current tree: (1) norm reductions auto-promote fp16/bf16 to fp32 with a float64 cross-leaf squared-norm accumulator and a two-stage blocked per-leaf reduction (_pytree.py:81-103, 145-265); (2) the clip scale is shrunk by a computed roundoff guard so norm(output) <= clipping_norm holds on the values as stored (_guard_scale/_finalize_scale, _pytree.py:106-142) - empirically confirmed per-example stored norms <= 1.0 in bf16; (3) microbatch accumulation holds the running sum at the promoted compute dtype and casts to the output dtype exactly once (_MicrobatchAccumulator, _clipped_fun.py:137-191), matching the non-microbatch _sum_clipped_tensor (:115-134) - empirically confirmed bit-exact parity (max abs diff 0.0) between microbatch_size=7 and full-batch in bf16 for both the gradient and the second-moment stream. AUTO-S goes through the same guarded machinery. Residual (pre-existing, inherent): the final /normalize_by and the fp32->bf16 output downcast happen after the guard, one unguarded ~2^-9 relative rounding common to all DP-SGD implementations.

statuses.title: Derive distributed synchronization from schemas, not rank-local values

The shipped test _worker_sync_aux_empty_vs_per_group hand-builds a float 0.5 on the non-empty rank and so misses the real aux shape.

statuses.title: Preserve integer and float64 exactness in scalar reductions
statuses.note: Verified: reduce_scalar (_state.py:122-181) routes ints through an exact torch.int64 collective (bool rejected), supports compute_dtype float64, and computes integer means from an exact integer sum; assert_scalar_equal (:39-75) compares ints with == (no isclose rtol); sync_object's assert_equal/assert_optional_equal pass atol=0/rtol=0 with float64 for floats (:441-447, :464-470). statuses.title: Do not retry collectives after callback TypeError
statuses.note: The retry ('except TypeError: result = field_op(value)') is gone: sync_object now invokes a field callable exactly once as fn(value, device) (_state.py:423-424) and exceptions propagate unchanged, so a callable that issues collectives issues them exactly once — a callable that all-reduces then raises can no longer issue a second, schedule-desynchronizing collective via the retry. _validate_field_op (:331-361) rejects wrong-arity callables (signature.bind(None, None)) and bad op strings before any collective begins. Verified live: the 2-rank gloo regression in engine_ddp_helpers.py (_reduce_then_fail asserts reductions == [world_size] after the TypeError) passes; grep confirms no other except-TypeError-retry pattern near collectives survives in packages/*/src (remaining handlers are local len()-probes in _eval.py/_dp_trainer.py with no collectives).

statuses.title: Make Adafactor epsilon floors scale-aware
statuses.note: All three eps_root sites are now scale-relative: _adafactor.py:141-146 clamps r_mean to eps_root*v_row.mean() (inner clamp 1e-30 guards the zero-state first step), :247-248 clamps the factored denominator to eps_root*sqrt(mean(v_hat)), :259-260 the scalar-branch denominator to eps_root*sqrt(mean(v_eff)). Genuinely scale-invariant, not a different constant: multiplying gradients by k scales v_* by k^2 and every floor by k, so the update is invariant. Verified empirically -- update norms identical (to 6 decimals) for gradient scales 1.0, 1e-4, 1e-8, and 1e-12 (only eps_grad=1e-30 breaks invariance below ~1e-12, genuine underflow guarding). The commit's regression tests (TestScaleAware, 4 tests) assert non-collapse at DP scale, non-equivalence to RMS-SGD, scale invariance, and BC activity at DP scale; all 23 test_adafactor.py tests pass on the current tree.

findings.title: Schedule-blind strategy equality lets the composition merge collapse distinct-lr-schedule MF processes
findings.claim: Residual of closed issue #332: all four MF strategy dataclasses declare lr_schedule as field(default=None, compare=False) (_band_mf.py:110, _bisr.py:160, _lambda_cgd.py:119, _blt.py:132), so MfGaussian.__eq__/__hash__ (plain dataclass semantics comparing the strategy field) are blind to the schedule, while the schedule genuinely changes the strategy's coefficients and priced sensitivity since #529. DpProcess.__or__'s same-leaf merge (opaque-accounting core/_base.py:474-477: 'if left_leaf == right_leaf: return Repeated(left_leaf, left_count + right_count)') therefore collapses two processes differing only in lr_schedule into K repetitions of the LEFT one, silently pricing the second phase at the first phase's schedule.
findings.failure_scenario: A user composes two MF training phases with identical noise_multiplier/bands/momentum but different lr schedules: mf_gaussian(1.0, band_mf_strategy(bands=4, lr_schedule=s1)) | mf_gaussian(1.0, band_mf_strategy(bands=4, lr_schedule=s2)) becomes Repeated(phase1, 2); the reported epsilon corresponds to two copies of the s1-weighted sensitivity and can understate the true privacy loss when s2's weighting yields larger sensitivity. The PLD cache is NOT affected (its key materializes the schedule via strategy_cache_key), which makes the eq-path collapse easy to miss in cache-focused tests.
evidence: _band_mf.py:110: 'lr_schedule: Schedule | None = field(default=None, compare=False)' inside @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) BandMfStrategy - dataclass semantics exclude compare=False fields from __eq__ and __hash__
_band_mf.py:111-127: coefficients() passes _lr_key(self.lr_schedule, n_steps) into _band_mf_coefficients_cached and sensitivity() is float(coefs.norm()) - the schedule changes the priced sensitivity
core/_base.py:474-477: '__or__' direct merge on 'left_leaf == right_leaf' returning Repeated(left_leaf, ...), discarding the right process object entirely
_mf_gaussian.py:41-75: MfGaussian is a default-eq frozen dataclass whose _pld_cache_key (but not __eq__) goes through strategy_cache_key/materialize_schedule (_schedule_fingerprint.py:12-43)
findings.fix_sketch: Either include a schedule fingerprint in strategy equality (drop compare=False in favor of a materialization-stable token, or a custom __eq__ comparing _lr_key at the declared horizon), or make DpProcess.__or__'s merge use _pld_cache_key-style resolved identity instead of dataclass __eq__ for leaves that defer resolution.

findings.claim: The fix for closed issue #331 (OPQ-182, commit 23c0dbc7) converted balls-in-bins MC to fixed 1024-sample shards, but the sibling b-min-sep Monte Carlo driver in the same crate still partitions by the runtime worker count: `let n_threads = rayon::current_num_threads().max(1); let samples_per_thread = num_samples / n_threads;` with per-thread RNGs `StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed.wrapping_add(tid as u64))` (remove) and `seed.wrapping_add(1000 + tid as u64)` (add). findings.title: self-convolution exponent silently truncated to u32 on the budgeted circular path
findings.claim: After the #341/#528 fixes, one overflow survives: `*c = c.powu(count as u32);` truncates count modulo 2^32. For a multi-element PMF with count > u32::MAX the linear strategy is always rejected (full_result_len > 2^32 > MAX_LINEAR_FFT_SIZE), but when tail budgets are set the circular fallback is taken and the frequency spectrum is raised to the WRONG (wrapped) power, silently composing count mod 2^32 steps instead of count - an epsilon underreport by orders of magnitude. Unreachable from Python: python/pld.rs:31-39 composition_count caps count at u32::MAX with OverflowError. Reachable only via the Rust crate's public self_convolve/self_convolve_with_bounds/Pmf::self_compose API (rlib consumers).
findings.failure_scenario: A Rust-level consumer (the crate builds as rlib and these functions are pub) calls pmf.with_tail_budgets(1e-15, 1e-15).self_compose(2^32 + 10) on a two-element PMF: the Chernoff window is small, the circular FFT proceeds, and the result is the 10-fold composition presented as the (2^32+10)-fold one, with no error.
evidence: fft.rs:316-318: `for c in a_freq.iter_mut() { *c = c.powu(count as u32); }` - rustfft Complex::powu takes u32; `count as u32` wraps

fft.rs:187-193 checks usize overflow of the result length but a.len()=2, count=2^32+10 gives full_result_len ~ 2^32+11 which fits usize and merely forces the circular branch when allow_circular_fallback is true

python/pld.rs:31-39: `let count = u32::try_from(count).map_err(|_| overflow())?;` - the Python surface is safe, tested by test_singleton_self_convolution_supports_maximum_exponent for the singleton path only
All in-crate call sites (random_allocation.rs:478,671,727; mechanisms/*.rs) pass parameter-bounded counts
findings.fix_sketch: Guard in self_convolve_with_bounds: `if count > u32::MAX as usize { return Err(...) }` (mirroring the Python boundary), or use repeated squaring of the spectrum with a usize exponent as pow_usize already does for the singleton case.

findings.title: Per-group adaptive clip sync permutes group counts across ranks; thresholds silently diverge
findings.claim: sync_adaptive_clip_state reduces per-group clipped counts positionally by iterating state._num_clipped.items() ('for gname, local_count in state._num_clipped.items(): global_num_clipped[gname] = reduce_scalar(local_count, op="sum")'), but the dict's key order is code-path-dependent: the non-empty stats path (return_aux=False default) stores counts in leaf-traversal group order (engine _compute_clipping_stats builds counts iterating group_norms_dict, packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_fun.py:500-503, ordered by group first-occurrence along optree paths, _pytree.py:268-283), while the empty-batch path stores dict.fromkeys(initial_clipping_norm.values, 0.0) in PerGroup.values construction order (_adaptive.py:357-360) and the return_aux path uses sorted() order (_adaptive.py:527). When one rank draws an empty batch (routine under Poisson/DDP, guaranteed under RandomAllocationSampler) and PerGroup.values order differs from leaf order (arbitrary user pattern order via per_group()), the positionally-matched all_reduce sums counts of DIFFERENT groups and each rank assigns the sums to differently-ordered keys: global counts are permuted on the empty rank and the recomputed per-group thresholds diverge across ranks with no error. This is closed issue #368's defect class (sync derived from rank-local values, not a schema) surviving in the dpsgd sibling path.
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced live (2-rank Gloo): PerGroup(groups={'a_weight':'W','b_bias':'B'}, values={'B':1000.0,'W':1.0}), return_aux=False, rank 0 non-empty (4 examples, all W clipped), rank 1 empty. After sync: rank 0 global counts {'W':4,'B':0} (correct), rank 1 {'B':4,'W':0} (permuted); next thresholds W=1.1008 on rank 0 vs W=0.9013 on rank 1. From then on ranks clip records at different thresholds and scale noise to different max_norms while summing gradients into one model: silent training corruption, and the noise std applied on the low-threshold rank is below the sensitivity actually enforced on the other rank, so released iterates are under-noised relative to the accounted mechanism.

findings.title: AdaClip accounting accepts invalid parameters on direct construction; num_groups=0 silently prices adaptive clipping as free
findings.claim: The #336/#516 remediation pattern (validate in __post_init__ so direct construction and deserialization cannot pass invalid state to the native call) was applied to Poisson, ParallelPoisson, RandomAllocation and KOutOfT but not to the sibling AdaClip dataclass, which has no __post_init__. Direct construction (or a hand-edited/corrupted serialized process, cf. closed #342 which made every Budget serializable) accepts num_groups=0, negative fraction_noise_std, and negative expected_batch_size. num_groups=0 makes adaclip_sensitivity return z-tilde = z (the K/(4*sigma_b^2) term vanishes), so effective_noise_multiplier equals the bare Gaussian's and the quantile-query privacy cost is charged as zero; negative sigma_b inputs enter squared and are silently accepted.
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced: AdaClip(inner=Gaussian(1.1), fraction_noise_std=0.05, expected_batch_size=250.0, num_groups=0) yields z_eff=1.1 and poisson(...).pld().epsilon_at(1e-5)=0.14229 vs the correctly-charged 0.14276 — the accountant reports an epsilon omitting the adaptive-clipping release entirely, with no warning. fraction_noise_std=-0.05 and expected_batch_size=-250.0 are likewise accepted (sign lost in the square). A state dict restored with a zeroed num_groups silently under-reports epsilon while the runtime keeps releasing noisy quantile statistics.

contrast: Poisson.__post_init__ (_poisson.py:37-61), ParallelPoisson.__post_init__ (_parallel_poisson.py:23-36), RandomAllocation.__post_init__ (_random_allocation.py:67-77), KOutOfT.__post_init__ (_k_out_of_t.py:40-47) all validate for exactly this reason

findings.fix_sketch: Add AdaClip.__post_init__ mirroring the factory checks (fraction_noise_std > 0, expected_batch_size > 0, num_groups >= 1 and integral), matching the pattern already applied to the other dpsgd accounting dataclasses; consider the same for Gaussian (negative noise_multiplier currently only fails later inside the native call).

findings.title: Sampler RNG streams are exempt from the #728 namespaced-root convention and can collide byte-identically
findings.claim: Commit 6f6d132a (#728) namespaced every noise-mechanism and auditing RNG stream under a unique string root, and docs/reference/rng.md:208-212 states the convention exists because 'fold_in(key, step) is what every mechanism writes first'. The dpsgd samplers were left out: PoissonSampler seeds numpy directly from key.seed (_poisson.py:108), KOutOfTSampler from self._key.seed (_k_out_of_t.py:58), and RandomAllocationSampler derives each epoch's assignment from the bare integer fold fold_in(self._key, epoch) (_random_allocation.py:125). The documented per-rank Poisson derivation fold_in(key, rank) (_poisson.py:42-49) is byte-identical key material to RandomAllocationSampler's epoch derivation for rank==epoch, and both consume it through the same numpy PCG64 family, so two samplers handed one base key draw correlated (identical) inclusion randomness. Sampler randomness IS the amplification randomness, so a collision correlates subsampling across components with nothing to signal it.
findings.failure_scenario: A user who trusts the RNG guide's mechanism-root guarantee and reuses one base key for a per-rank PoissonSampler (fold_in(K, rank)) and a RandomAllocationSampler (internally fold_in(K, epoch)) gets rank r's Poisson stream seeded identically to RA epoch r's assignment: the two subsampling processes are deterministically coupled, violating the independence the amplification analyses assume. No shipped example hits this today, so current epsilon values are unaffected; the exposure is the forward-looking class the audit flagged as OPQ-128 and the team fixed for auditing in #374/#728.

packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/sampling/_poisson.py:108 'self.generator = np.random.default_rng(key.seed)' plus docstring :42-49 recommending fold_in(key, rank)
packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/sampling/_k_out_of_t.py:58 'rng = np.random.default_rng(self._key.seed)'

Since split(key, n) is defined as fold_in(key, i), the lambda-CGD noise released at step t is byte-identical to a torch draw from the caller's split(base)[t] key — the exact aliasing the fix eliminated everywhere else, and the exact invariant the new enforcement test states ('Any stream root Opaque derives for itself must be a namespaced string', packages/opaque-engine/tests/rng/test_stream_root_namespacing.py:1-10). That test cannot catch lambda-CGD because the mechanism declares no root constant at all. docs/reference/rng.md:220 falsely lists 'opaque.dpftrl.mf_gaussian' as rooting mf_gaussian_noise — untrue when the strategy is LambdaCgdStrategy (the dispatcher special-cases it into _make_lambda_cgd_noise with the raw user key).

Demonstrated: with lambda_=0.0, the mechanism's step-0 and step-1 released noise vectors are torch.equal to torch.randn drawn from generator_from_key(split(base)[0]) and [1]. findings.title: BISR runtime keeps n_steps-1 gradient-sized buffers, contradicting the documented p-1-vector / PRNG-replay design
findings.claim: The #360 fix (2507548b) made the BISR runtime operator mathematically exact by handing the DENSE length-n_steps strategy coefficients to inverse_as_streaming_matrix (_bisr.py:200: 'strategy_coefs = _native().bisr_strategy_coefficients(inv, n_steps)'), whose forward-substitution state is (bands-1, *grad_shape) with bands = len(coef) = n_steps (_toeplitz.py:239-244 'return zero.unsqueeze(0).expand(bands - 1, *zero.shape).clone()'). BISR's whole point is that C^{-1} is banded with p coefficients — the noise row is a p-term convolution of past iid draws computable with p-1 buffers or zero-memory PRNG replay — yet the implementation stores n_steps-1 full gradient copies and does O(n_steps * d) work per step. docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/bisr.md still documents the intended design (':10 Memory: p-1 noise vectors (via PRNG replay or small buffer)', ':96', ':109'). None of that matches the code.
findings.failure_scenario: Measured on this tree: bisr_strategy(bandwidth=4), n_steps=512, 1M-param model -> streaming state tensor (511, 1000000) = 2.04 GB and 4.27 s per noise step on CPU; both scale linearly in n_steps. A realistic LLM run (n_steps=10k, 1B params) needs ~40 TB of noise state — the mechanism OOMs at any real scale, and at toy scale silently pays O(n_steps) memory/time while the user believes the documented p-1-vector cost. Correctness of released noise is unaffected (operator verified exact).
evidence: packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_bisr.py:200 'strategy_coefs = _native().bisr_strategy_coefficients(inv, n_steps)' passed as coef to inverse_as_streaming_matrix
packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_toeplitz.py:239-244 init state = (bands-1, *shape) with bands = coef.shape[0]
Executed: state tensors [(), (511, 1000000)] -> 2.04 GB; one noise step 4.27 s (n=512, d=1e6, p=4)
docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/bisr.md:10,96,109 claim p-1 vectors / PRNG replay
Runtime operator exactness separately verified: materialize() == exact banded C^{-1} (and D*C^{-1} when normalized), max err 0.0 at n=12
findings.fix_sketch: Apply the banded C^{-1} directly: keep the last p-1 iid draws (ring buffer keyed like the streaming engine's per-step generators, or PRNG-replay them as lambda-CGD does) and emit sum_k inv_c[k] * z_{t-k}, times the column-norm diagonal d_t when normalized. That is O(p) buffers and O(p*d) per step and matches the docs; the current dense forward-substitution path can remain as a cross-check in tests.

findings.title: lr_schedule is compare=False, so the accountant's structural merge collapses MF mechanisms with different schedules
findings.claim: All four schedule-carrying strategies declare 'lr_schedule: Schedule | None = field(default=None, compare=False)' (_band_mf.py:110, _bisr.py:160, _blt.py:132, _lambda_cgd.py:119). The #332/#362 remediation keyed the PLD caches by materialized schedules (strategy_cache_key), but DpProcess.__or__ merges accountant steps by structural equality (packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_base.py:460-477: 'if left_leaf == right_leaf: return Repeated(left_leaf, left_count + right_count)'), and dataclass equality ignores compare=False fields. Two per-step DP-FTRL processes that differ only in lr_schedule therefore compare equal and merge, silently pricing every step under the FIRST process's schedule-weighted Gram. Possible overlap with open issue #319 ('Restore DP-FTRL mechanism and strategy invariants'), but this specific residual is a direct leftover of the closed #332/#362 fixes, which repaired cache keys while leaving merge identity schedule-blind.
findings.failure_scenario: Demonstrated on this tree: pa = per_step(balls_in_bins(mf_gaussian(1.0, lambda_cgd_strategy(lambda_=0.5, lr_schedule=cosine)), num_bins=4, n_steps=8)) and pb identical except lr_schedule=constant satisfy pa == pb; pa | pb returns Repeated(count=2) built on pa's leaf, although the two mechanisms' true full-horizon epsilons differ (3.5241 vs 3.6750 at delta=1e-5). A user composing training phases with different LR schedules in one Accountant (acct |= step across phases — the documented idiom) gets an epsilon computed entirely from the first phase's schedule; depending on the schedules the reported epsilon can understate the true cost.
evidence: grep: lr_schedule compare=False at _band_mf.py:110, _bisr.py:160, _blt.py:132, _lambda_cgd.py:119
packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_base.py:473-477 merge on structural equality
Executed repro: pa == pb -> True; (pa | pb) -> Repeated count=2; eps(cosine)=3.5241 vs eps(constant)=3.6750
Contrast: _pld_cache_key/strategy_cache_key DO distinguish the schedules (verified strategy_cache_key(s_plain, n) != strategy_cache_key(s_lr, n)) — only the equality/merge path is blind
findings.fix_sketch: Make schedule identity participate in strategy equality: either drop compare=False (Schedule recipes are frozen dataclasses that compare structurally; raw callables fall back to identity), or override __eq__ on the strategies to compare materialize_schedule fingerprints; alternatively have DpProcess.__or__ refuse to merge leaves whose _pld_cache_key() differ.

findings.title: Noise-stream continuity tests cover only 2 of 7 noise-state shapes; trainer-level resume test still checks only step count and epsilon
findings.claim: The #426 fix (commit 4be102ee) added TestNoiseStreamContinuity for gaussian_noise and band_mf only. BLT (buffered streaming state), BISR (dense forward-substitution state), BSR, lambda-CGD (PRNG replay), identity, and the paired SecondMomentMFNoiseState have no continuity regression test, and the end-to-end resume test (test_dpftrl_trainer_smoke.py:240-298) still asserts only out2.global_step == out1.global_step and epsilon approx-equality — both insensitive to noise-state restoration, which is the precise gap OPQ-157 identified. I verified by direct execution that the continuity invariant currently HOLDS for all six strategies and the second-moment state (bit-exact resumed draws through state_dict/torch.save/from_state_dict), so this is regression protection, not a live defect.
findings.failure_scenario: A future refactor of BLT buffer serialization, the BISR streaming state, or lambda-CGD's key derivation (e.g. the namespacing fix proposed in the lambda-CGD finding) could silently reset or fork the noise stream on resume; no test would fail, and a resumed run would replay already-released noise (correlated releases the accountant never modeled) or diverge from the accounted mechanism.
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/tests/opaque_transformers/test_checkpoint_helpers.py:283-300 — only gaussian_noise and band_mf_strategy parametrizations
packages/opaque-transformers/tests/opaque_transformers/test_dpftrl_trainer_smoke.py:291-298 — resume assertions limited to global_step and privacy_epsilon (rel=1e-3)
Executed: continuity bit-exact for identity/band_mf/blt/bisr/bsr/lambda_cgd and SecondMomentMFNoiseState on this tree
findings.fix_sketch: Parametrize _assert_continuity over all mf strategies (they share the make_noise closure shape) plus a paired second-moment case, and add one trainer-level test comparing final model parameters of a straight-through run vs checkpoint+resume at noise_multiplier > 0 (bit-identical on CPU with fixed seeds).

findings.title: Loss-scale backoff/growth is an unaccounted data-dependent adaptive choice the docs claim is fully accounted
findings.claim: The #350 fix removes the data-dependent skip, but the replacement pattern feeds the raw, un-noised private statistic stats.all_finite into LossScaler.update (docs/user-guide/precision.md:99, _loss_scaler.py:185-195), so the scale at step t+1 is a function of private data at step t that was never released or accounted. The scale changes which per-example gradients overflow and are zeroed by clip_pytree's sanitization (_pytree.py:520-527), so under add/remove adjacency one record's presence at step t can flip the scale at t+1 and thereby change other records' released contributions at t+1 by up to C each - per-step sensitivity conditioned on a shared transcript is no longer C, and per-step PLD composition (which allows adaptivity only through released outputs) does not strictly cover the composed mechanism. docs/user-guide/precision.md:102-106 asserts the overflow path is fully 'composed into the accountant'; the pre-fix warning that this is 'not free privacy-wise' was deleted in 18f67eac.
findings.failure_scenario: fp16 functional-API training following the documented recipe (loss_scaler + return_stats + accountant). After neighboring datasets diverge in a single overflow event, the backoff (or delayed growth) makes the two runs use different scales on all subsequent steps; examples whose scaled gradients sit near the fp16 overflow boundary are zeroed in one run and kept in the other, changing the released noisy gradients by more than the accounted sensitivity C while the reported epsilon is unchanged.
evidence: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/precision/_loss_scaler.py:185-195 - update(state, grads_were_finite) consumes the raw finiteness bit and moves scale by growth/backoff factors

docs/user-guide/precision.md:99 'scaler_state = scaler.update(scaler_state, stats.all_finite)' and :102-106 'the zero contribution is still noised, optimized, and composed into the accountant. The stats then back off the next loss scale.'
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_pytree.py:520-527 - non-finite leaves are zeroed, making the released contribution scale-dependent exactly when overflow flips
git show 18f67eac - deleted 'A skip is data-dependent and is not free privacy-wise. Unless separately analyzed, advance accounting on a public fixed schedule.'
findings.fix_sketch: Either drive the scale schedule from a released (noised) overflow statistic or a public schedule, or document that stats.all_finite-driven scaling is an adaptive query outside the stated guarantee and quantify/gate it the way adaptive clipping is gated for MF mechanisms.

findings.title: The #352 wrapper-blindness pattern survives in unscale_grads and global_norm (silent no-op / silent 0.0 on ClippedPytree)
findings.claim: Issue #352 was fixed only for all_finite. Its siblings still treat DP wrapper types as opaque leaves: LossScaler.unscale_grads uses bare optree tree_map (_loss_scaler.py:172-183 via opaque.pytree.tree_map, pytree.py:126-142), and ClippedPytree/NoisedPytree are unregistered dataclasses, so unscale_grads(ClippedPytree, state) returns the wrapper object unchanged without unscaling anything - empirically confirmed (returned object is the input, leaf value 8.0 unchanged with scale=4). Likewise opaque.pytree.global_norm(ClippedPytree) silently returns 0.0 because tree_leaves finds no tensor leaves - empirically confirmed (0.0 vs 5.0 on the unwrapped pytree).
findings.failure_scenario: A user following the torch.amp.GradScaler mental model calls scaler.unscale_grads on the ClippedPytree returned by grad_fn (instead of wiring it as pre_clipping_transform): the call silently no-ops, gradients remain grads of the scaled loss clipped at C (clipping rate ~100%, silently wrong training configuration). A user logging global_norm(clipped_grads) gets a constant 0.0 and debugs the wrong thing. Neither path raises.
evidence: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/precision/_loss_scaler.py:172-183 - unscale_grads uses tree_map; wrappers are leaves and fail the isinstance(t, torch.Tensor) test
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/pytree.py:122-123, 142 - tree_leaves/tree_map are bare optree; ClippedPytree is not registered as a pytree node
empirical: unscale_grads(clipped({'g': tensor([8.0])}, max_norm=1.0), state) with scale=4 returns the same object with 8.0 intact; global_norm(clipped({'g': [3,4]}, max_norm=1.0)) == 0.0
findings.fix_sketch: Mirror the all_finite fix: have unscale_grads and global_norm unwrap ClippedPytree/NoisedPytree/SecondMomentClippingOutput (unscale should also rescale max_norm metadata, or raise TypeError directing the caller to .pytree, as ClippedPytree.__add__ already does for unsupported ops).

findings.title: Empty-batch short-circuit ignores dtype= and pre_clipping_transform structure, breaking step-shape stability under Poisson sampling
findings.claim: _empty_batch_response builds zero gradients with zero_grads_like(args, argnums) (_clipped_grad.py:218, _helpers.py:76-86), which copies the parameter pytree's structure and dtype, while non-empty steps return gradients in the configured output dtype and in whatever structure pre_clipping_transform produces (documented as allowed to change structure, _clipped_grad.py:170-175). Empirically confirmed on the current tree: with dtype=torch.float32 and bf16 params, a non-empty batch returns fp32 and an empty batch returns bf16; with a structure-changing pre_clipping_transform, a non-empty batch returns a dict and an empty batch returns a bare Tensor. adaptive_clipped_grad's own empty-batch path (_adaptive.py:402-415) has the same behavior, and auto_clipped_grad inherits it.
findings.failure_scenario: Poisson sampling routinely produces empty batches; the empty-batch path exists precisely so those steps look like every other step. A run configured with dtype= or a structure-changing pre_clipping_transform gets a differently-shaped/typed ClippedPytree on empty steps: MF noise (which latches metadata on first call) or torchopt optimizer state initialized from a non-empty step then errors or silently casts when an empty step arrives - and if the FIRST step is empty, everything downstream latches the wrong template.
evidence: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_grad.py:216-230 - zeros = zero_grads_like(args, argnums_tuple); no dtype cast, no pre_clipping_transform application
empirical: dtype=torch.float32, bf16 params -> non-empty dtype torch.float32, empty dtype torch.bfloat16; pre_clipping_transform=lambda g: {'g': g} -> non-empty structure dict, empty structure Tensor
packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/clipping/_adaptive.py:402-415 - same zero_grads_like short-circuit
findings.fix_sketch: In the empty-batch path, apply pre_clipping_transform to the zero pytree and cast leaves to the configured output dtype, in clipped_grad, adaptive_clipped_grad, and auto_clipped_grad alike; or reject structure-changing transforms/dtype overrides at factory time when they cannot be honored on empty batches.

findings.title: Per-group clipping crashes DDP training on any partially-empty Poisson round
findings.claim: The #368 empty-batch fix left the aux schema itself data-dependent under per-group clipping: the empty-batch short-circuit hardcodes clipping_rate=0.0 while the non-empty per-group path emits clipping_rate=None, so _sync_clipping_rate's new presence check raises RuntimeError on every rank the first time some-but-not-all ranks draw an empty Poisson batch.
findings.failure_scenario: DPTrainer with TrainingArguments.clipping_norm={...} (per-group dict; fixed and adaptive modes both affected) + DDP + Poisson sampling. On a step where one rank's Poisson draw is empty and another's is not, sync(aux) in training_step (_dp_trainer.py:2104) raises 'Clipped auxiliary clipping_rate presence mismatch across ranks.' on every rank and the training run dies mid-stream. Reproduced live on 2-rank gloo: rank 0 empty -> clipping_rate=0.0, rank 1 batch of 4 -> clipping_rate=None, both ranks raise (no hang — follow-up collective still works — so it is a fail-closed crash, not silent corruption).
evidence: _clipped_grad.py:238 (empty-batch aux): 'clipping_rate=0.0,' — unconditional, even when clipping_norm is a PerGroup

_clipped_fun.py:852-856 (non-empty aux): 'clipping_rate=(stats.clipping_rate if isinstance(stats.clipping_rate, float) or stats.clipping_rate is None else None)' — per-group rates are a dict, so the aux field becomes None

engine/clipping/_distributed.py:224-230: 'local_presence = int(clipping_rate is not None); ... if min_presence != max_presence: raise RuntimeError("Clipped auxiliary clipping_rate presence mismatch across ranks.")'
dpsgd/clipping/_adaptive.py:423 empty path 'clipping_rate=0.0' vs :617 non-empty 'clipping_rate=aux.clipping_rate if aux is not None else None' — adaptive per-group has the same divergence
Reachability: _dp_trainer.py:1408-1421 builds a PerGroup clip_norm from the documented clipping_norm dict; :4177-4185 passes it to clipped_grad(return_aux=True); :2099-2104 calls sync under DDP

Live 2-rank gloo repro output: 'rank 0: local clipping_rate=0.0 bs=0 / rank 1: local clipping_rate=None bs=4 / both ranks: SYNC RAISED RuntimeError: Clipped auxiliary clipping_rate presence mismatch across ranks.'

The shipped regression test _worker_sync_aux_empty_vs_per_group (engine_ddp_helpers.py:673-715) hand-builds the non-empty rank with clipping_rate=0.5 (a float), which real per-group clipped_grad never produces — the test passes while the real path crashes
findings.fix_sketch: Make aux clipping_rate presence a function of the clipping schema, not the batch: in _empty_batch_response (and the adaptive empty path) emit clipping_rate=None when clipping_norm is a PerGroup (matching the non-empty aux), or have _sync_clipping_rate derive presence from the clip configuration. Extend _worker_sync_aux_empty_vs_per_group to build both auxes through the real clipped_grad(PerGroup, return_aux=True) instead of hand-crafting fields.

findings.title: Distributed CI lane passes silently if its test selection collapses to zero
findings.claim: The blocking two-rank lane added for #366/#328 sets allow-empty-test-selection:true, and the runner converts pytest exit code 5 (no tests collected) into success per package, so a refactor that renames/unmarks the 'distributed' tests or moves them out of the scanned package paths turns the desync-regression lane green with zero tests executed.
findings.failure_scenario: A marker rename (e.g. 'distributed' -> 'ddp'), a conftest change that deselects the ddp directories, or moving the spawn tests out of packages/*/tests makes every suite in the linux-distributed job exit 5; run_python_test_package.sh logs '::notice::No tests matched' and exits 0; the branch-protection 'Python tests' gate sees success. The exact regression class this lane exists to block (OPQ-001-style collective desync) can then reland invisibly — the failure mode the original audit called out for OPQ-051.
evidence: .github/workflows/pr.yml:76-85: python-tests-distributed passes 'allow-empty-test-selection: true' with pytest-marker 'distributed and not cuda' (same in ci.yml:41-50 and prepare-release-implementation.yml:307-317)
.github/scripts/run_python_test_package.sh:40-43: 'if [[ "$status" -eq 5 && "$ALLOW_EMPTY_TEST_SELECTION" == "true" ]]; then echo "::notice::No tests matched..."; exit 0; fi'
No step in python-tests.yml asserts that at least one suite in the distributed job actually collected tests (TEST_RESULTS_FILE is written but never checked for non-emptiness)
findings.fix_sketch: For the distributed lane, require a minimum collected-test count: either drop allow-empty-test-selection and give every package at least one distributed test, or add a post-loop check that TEST_RESULTS_FILE is non-empty for the suites known to carry distributed tests (engine, dpsgd, dpftrl, optimizers, alignment, transformers).

findings.title: Optimizer-state drift audit marshals float64 fingerprints through float32 collectives with rtol=1e-5
findings.claim: Residual of #365: _assert_tensor_fingerprint_equal computes (sum, sumsq, min, max) in double precision but compares them via assert_scalar_equal without compute_dtype, so the collective runs at the float32 default with atol=1e-8/rtol=1e-5 — cross-rank optimizer-state drift below roughly 1e-5 relative (or below float32 resolution for large sums, ~2^-24 relative) passes an audit whose stated purpose is exactly drift detection.
findings.failure_scenario: Two ranks' Adam second-moment tensors diverge by a small relative amount (e.g. a non-deterministic kernel introduces 1e-6-relative drift that compounds over thousands of steps). sync_optimizer_state fingerprints each tensor, but min/max reduction of the float64 stats happens in float32 and the isclose check uses rtol=1e-5, so the audit stays silent while parameters slowly de-synchronize.
evidence: optimizers/distributed.py:98-103: 't = tensor.detach().double(); assert_scalar_equal(float(t.sum().item()), name=...)' — no compute_dtype argument on any of the five calls

engine/distributed/_state.py:65: 'dtype = compute_dtype or torch.float32' and :174: tensor dtype 'compute_dtype or torch.float32' — the float path defaults to float32 marshalling with atol=1e-8, rtol=1e-5

The module's own docstring (optimizers/distributed.py:85-93) says the fingerprint exists because 'drift detection is the entire point'; the master-list OPQ-049 note said float32 marshalling 'partially defeats' the audit — the integer half was fixed by #365 (ints now exact int64), the float half was not
findings.fix_sketch: Pass compute_dtype=torch.float64 and atol=0.0/rtol=0.0 (or a deliberately tiny tolerance) on the five assert_scalar_equal calls in _assert_tensor_fingerprint_equal, mirroring what sync_object's assert_equal path already does for float fields.

findings.title: DPTrainer never consults ScheduleFreeState.x: schedule-free eval and checkpoints use the wrong weight sequence
findings.claim: DPTrainer accepts optim='schedule_free' and the HF alias 'schedule_free_radam' (_optim.py:55, :94), but no code in opaque-transformers reads ScheduleFreeState.x -- grep for ScheduleFreeState/schedule_free across the package hits only the factory table and _build_schedule_free. The trainer therefore evaluates, checkpoints, and saves the y_t forward-pass iterate, which the wrapper's own module docstring (_schedule_free.py:43-45) says 'would defeat the purpose of schedule-free averaging'. Issue #408 was closed by documenting opt_state.x as the accessor, but through the trainer that accessor is never used and the documented save/eval contract is unattainable. docs/reference/transformers.md:233-234 lists schedule_free as a supported optim with no caveat.
findings.failure_scenario: A user sets optim='schedule_free' (or TrainingArguments.from_hf with HF's schedule_free_radam) expecting the published Polyak-averaged x_t -- the entire point of the method, and under DP the source of the ~Var/n noise reduction the docs advertise. Every eval metric, best-model selection, and saved checkpoint instead reflects y_t = (1-beta)z_t + beta*x_t, which at beta=0.9 is still 10% raw noisy iterate; the noise-reduction benefit is silently lost and reported eval numbers do not describe the model a library user following docs/reference/optimizers.md:196-197 would export.
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_optim.py:55: '"schedule_free": opaque_opt.schedule_free,' and :94: '"schedule_free_radam": ("schedule_free", {"base": "radam"}),'

grep -rn 'ScheduleFreeState|schedule_free' over packages/opaque-transformers/src returns only _optim.py and _training_arguments.py alias/doc lines -- zero consumers of .x in _dp_trainer.py, _checkpoint.py, _eval.py, _hub.py

packages/opaque-optimizers/src/opaque/api/optimizers/_schedule_free.py:42-47: 'Saving / evaluating against y_t would defeat the purpose... This is the dependency that gates schedule-free's usefulness through DPTrainer'
docs/reference/transformers.md:233-234 lists 'schedule_free' among supported optim values with no eval/save caveat
findings.fix_sketch: In DPTrainer, when the built optimizer is a schedule_free wrapper, swap model params to opt_state.x around evaluate()/save_model()/checkpoint export (and swap back), or refuse optim='schedule_free' with a message pointing at the library-level API until the trainer integration lands; at minimum add the caveat to docs/reference/transformers.md. May partially overlap open umbrella issues #321/#323, but neither names this specific gap.

findings.title: Adafactor module docstring misstates the BC default (says True, actual False) plus two stale/incorrect memory statements
findings.claim: Three docstring statements contradict the code: (1) lines 30-31 say noise_bias_correction 'defaults to ``True`` so BC is on by default' while the signature (line 303) is noise_bias_correction: bool = False and the arg docstring (line 335) correctly says False -- the module contradicts itself; (2) line 28 says the phi-EMA is subtracted 'with a positive floor', stale since the where-fallback semantics that b9faed0a documented in _bias_correction.py:20-31 (torch.where(corr>0, corr, v), no floor, _adafactor.py:238-239); (3) lines 6-7 say rank<2 tensors 'fall back to a scalar second moment' while _init_v_for_leaf:120 allocates torch.zeros_like(leaf) -- a full per-element tensor for vectors (paper-correct behavior, wrong description; also relevant to closed #406's memory-doc alignment).
findings.failure_scenario: A DP user reads the module doc (the file whose header sells the BC feature), concludes bias correction is already active, and trains with adafactor() defaults: the second-moment factors silently retain the +sigma^2 noise bias the docstring told them was being removed. No error, just the uncorrected optimizer the docs say they are not running.
evidence: _adafactor.py:30-31: '``noise_bias_correction=True`` activates this path; defaults to ``True`` so BC is on by default.'
_adafactor.py:303: 'noise_bias_correction: bool = False' and :335: 'Defaults to ``False``; Adafactor's relative-step per-tensor normalization already plays BC's role'
_adafactor.py:238-239: 'torch.where(corr_row > 0, corr_row, new_v_row)' -- fallback, not a positive floor
_adafactor.py:120: 'return (torch.zeros_like(leaf),)' for leaf.dim() < 2 -- per-element, not scalar
findings.fix_sketch: Rewrite the three sentences: default is False; subtraction falls back to the uncorrected factor where non-positive (cross-reference _bias_correction.py); rank<2 leaves keep a full per-element second moment (unfactored), matching the paper.

findings.title: Fabricated author list 'Defazio, Yaida, Cutkosky' survives the closed citation-repair sweep (#418 / OPQ-136)
findings.claim: OPQ-136's exact defect is still in the tree: _schedule_free.py:10 cites 'The Road Less Scheduled' (arXiv:2405.15682) as 'Defazio, Yaida, Cutkosky'. The real authors are Defazio, Yang, Mehta, Mishchenko, Khaled, Cutkosky; 'Yaida' (Sho Yaida) is not an author. The closed issue #418 'Audit and repair scholarly references' (commit 1d216fcd, which touched docs/reference/optimizers.md and three optimizer source files) missed this site -- the only place in the repo with the bad list, exactly as the audit recorded.
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer verifying the schedule-free implementation against the primary source attributes the paper to a nonexistent author combination; repo-wide grep for 'Yaida' confirms this is the sole remaining instance, so the audit's fix-one-site remedy was simply not applied.
evidence: _schedule_free.py:10: '    Defazio, Yaida, Cutkosky, "The Road Less Scheduled",'
grep -rn Yaida over the repo returns exactly this one line
AUDIT-master-list.md OPQ-136 records the identical defect and remedy; git show 1d216fcd contains no change to _schedule_free.py
findings.fix_sketch: Replace with 'Defazio, Yang, Mehta, Mishchenko, Khaled, Cutkosky' or 'Defazio et al.' (the form the other four citation sites already use).

findings.title: test_mode_switch_does_not_double_correct promises a reference comparison it never performs (the #405 vacuity pattern in a sibling file)
findings.claim: The test's docstring says the post-switch update 'must be finite and match what we'd get with phi forced to zero (no double correction)' and labels itself a regression test for the noisy_squared_grads-branch guards, but its only assertions after the switch are torch.isfinite(updates_after[k]).all() (line 338). It never computes the phi-zero reference or compares against it, so removing the 'noisy_squared_grads is None' guards in _adadelta.py:236/251 (re-introducing the double correction it guards against) would still pass as long as the update stays finite -- which a stale-phi subtraction with the where-fallback always is. b9faed0a (#405) eliminated this pattern in test_adagrad.py and test_rmsprop.py but did not touch this file.
findings.failure_scenario: A refactor drops the 'and noisy_squared_grads is None' condition from the phi_g/phi_dx correction guards; second-moment-substitution runs then subtract the stale phi EMAs from the already-debiased v_g/v_dx, skewing update magnitudes; the dedicated regression test stays green.
evidence: test_adadelta.py:333-335 comment: 'The output must be finite and match what we'd get with phi forced to zero (no double correction).'
test_adadelta.py:336-338: only 'assert torch.isfinite(updates_after[k]).all()' follows
_adadelta.py:249-253 and :269-273 are the guards the test claims to pin

findings.title: Dead bc_floor parameter left in Adadelta after the same cleanup removed it from Adagrad

findings.title: wpo_weights omits the WPO paper's per-token alignment term (and thus disagrees with TRL)
findings.claim: With DPOConfig(use_weighting=True), opaque's WPO pair weight is exp(mean masked per_token_logps) while both the cited WPO paper (arXiv:2406.11827, Eq. 2) and TRL 1.12 subtract the per-token alignment term log(sum_v p(v)^2) before averaging; the trainer multiplies per-example losses by this wrong weight, so WPO runs optimize a different objective than the paper the docstring claims to implement. The repo knows: test_trl_parity.py:518-526 marks the parity test as strict xfail instead of fixing the weight. Possibly inside the umbrella of OPEN issue #323 ('align trainer and alignment behavior with their public contracts'), but no open issue names WPO specifically.
findings.failure_scenario: User sets use_weighting=True (WPO) on DPOTrainer expecting the published WPO objective / TRL-equivalent behavior. _dpo_trainer.py:1139-1144 multiplies each pair's loss by _wpo_weight(chosen)*_wpo_weight(rejected) built from raw per-token logps; TRL computes aligned_logps = per_token_logps - (logsumexp(2x) - 2*logsumexp(x)) first (site-packages/trl/trainer/dpo_trainer.py:1595-1606). Since log(sum p^2) is in [-log V, 0] and varies per token, the two weights differ systematically, silently changing training dynamics and results versus the cited method.
evidence: packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/dpo/loss/_wpo.py:62-67 — 'avg_logp = (per_token_logps * mask).to(acc_dtype).sum(dim=-1); avg_logp = avg_logp / token_count...; return avg_logp.detach().exp()' — no logits, no alignment term.

packages/opaque-alignment/tests/test_trl_parity.py:518-526 — '@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason=("wpo_weights omits the WPO weight-alignment term log(sum_v p_v^2) that both TRL and the authors' reference implementation apply; the fix needs the logits, so it changes the public signature"))'.

installed trl 1.12.0 dpo_trainer.py:1595-1606 — 'lse2 = torch.logsumexp(2.0 * shift_logits, dim=-1); log_denom = lse2 - 2.0 * lse1; aligned_logps = (per_token_logps - log_denom) * shift_completion_mask; ... weights = torch.exp(mean_logps)'.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_dpo_trainer.py:1139-1144 applies the product of the two opaque weights to the per-example loss; _wpo_weight already receives chosen_out.logits, so the logits needed for the fix are available at that call site.
findings.fix_sketch: Add an optional logits (or log_denom) argument to wpo_weights and average (per_token_logps - (logsumexp(2*logits,-1) - 2*logsumexp(logits,-1))) under no_grad, mirroring TRL; wire _dpo_trainer._wpo_weight to pass the logits it already has; flip the xfail into a passing parity test. The weight stays detached and per-example, so DP clipping semantics are unchanged.

findings.title: Gemma2 SDPA shim is installed in the process-global attention registry, rerouting every model family

findings.title: _mu_at hang fix is symptom-level: strong attacks with >2000 canary guesses now raise RuntimeError, including the default epsilon_at surface at the documented 10000-canary scale
findings.claim: Commit 611faf51 (PR #299) fixes the infinite _mu_at hang by capping bracket doublings at 60 and raising RuntimeError — verified terminating in <1 s on the audit's pathological inputs (r=3000/u=0, r=5000/u=1400) — but it does not fix the underlying invariant (truncated ranks use v_k=0.5 regardless of mu at _gdp.py:333, so the Chernoff floor is n_trunc/2 and the p-value cannot rise above significance for any finite mu once u is well below n_trunc/2). Consequently every strong attack past _MAX_EXACT_RANKS=2000 guesses crashes instead of reporting an epsilon estimate.
findings.failure_scenario: A practitioner audits with m=10000 canaries — the scale the user guide's own canary-count table discusses — and the mechanism is badly under-noised, so the attack reaches 62% accuracy (u=3800). Measured in this session: OneRunEstimate.epsilon_at(delta=1e-5) (the DEFAULT dispatch, which routes to gdp() at _estimate.py:197) raises 'RuntimeError: cannot invert μ-GDP p-value for (m=10000, r=10000, u=3800)...' while u=3900 (61% accuracy) still returns mu=2.23. The audit's most alarming regime — exactly what auditing exists to detect — becomes a crash whose message suggests using fewer canaries; nothing in docs/user-guide/auditing.md or docs/reference/auditing.md mentions the 2000-rank truncation or this failure mode (grep for '2000|truncat' returns nothing). Fail-closed, so no wrong epsilon is emitted, but the limitation is undocumented and the root-cause fix the original audit proposed (a mu-dependent v_k bound for truncated ranks) was not implemented.

Session experiment: GdpMethod stub (5000,5000): u=3800 → RuntimeError; u=3900 → mu=2.2311; u=3950 → mu=1.6210
Termination verified: (1500,1500,u=0) RuntimeError in 0.6 s; (2500,2500,u=1400) in 0.7 s; boundary case (1000,1000,u=0), r=2000, converges to mu=5.98/eps=42.6 in 18 s at the default grid

docs/user-guide/auditing.md:215-228 discusses canary counts up to 1,000,000 with no mention of the mu-GDP 2000-guess power cap; AUDIT-master-list.md:299 records the audit's proposed root-cause fix ('fixing the μ-dependent v_k bound resolves two of them')
findings.fix_sketch: Implement a mu-dependent upper bound on v_k for truncated ranks (any valid bound that decays with mu restores p-value growth in mu and lets the search converge), or at minimum document the >2000-guess limitation in the auditing user guide and reference. Overlaps the broad open issue #327 (rebuild empirical auditing) but this concrete crash-at-strength behavior and its absence from docs are a specific residual of the #299 fix.

findings.title: fold_in's documented int/str domain disjointness is not structural: a 16-byte string collides with an integer fold
findings.claim: The #374/#728 RNG convention rests on the docstring guarantee that 'Integers and strings are hashed down disjoint paths ... no sequence of integer folds can reach a key derived through a string fold' (_engine.py:64-67), but _stable_hash64 encodes an int as exactly its 16-byte signed little-endian form plus a '|' separator and a str as its UTF-8 bytes plus '|' with no type tag, so any string whose UTF-8 encoding equals the 16-byte encoding of an int produces the identical key. Demonstrated in this session: fold_in(key(42), 1).seed == fold_in(key(42), "\\x01" + "\\x00"*15).seed is True.
findings.failure_scenario: All of Opaque's own stream roots are dotted-ASCII tags whose lengths differ from 16 bytes, so no internal stream collides today (the test_stream_root_namespacing.py guarantees hold). The exposure is the same forward-looking class OPQ-128 warned about: a third-party mechanism or future internal tag that happens to be a 16-byte string containing bytes aliasing a caller-integer fold would silently share a stream with an integer derivation, and the documented invariant users are told to rely on would not hold. No current epsilon is affected.
evidence: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/random/_engine.py:27-35 (_stable_hash64: int → to_bytes(16,'little',signed=True)+b'|', str → utf-8+b'|', no type discriminator)
Session repro: fold_in(key(42), 1) == fold_in(key(42), '\\x01'+'\\x00'*15) → True, contradicting _engine.py:64-65

packages/opaque-engine/tests/rng/test_stream_root_namespacing.py only probes integer folds in range(-64,512) and split(base,16) against the actual internal tags, so it cannot catch the encoding-aliasing class
findings.fix_sketch: Prefix a one-byte type tag in _stable_hash64 (e.g. b'i' before int bytes, b's' before str bytes) — a breaking key-derivation change like #728 itself, or soften the docstring to state the separation is encoding-based and NUL-containing 16-byte strings are reserved.

findings.title: mf_band + sampling_mode='poisson' pairs a plain Poisson sampler with cyclic-Poisson horizon accounting, underreporting epsilon
findings.claim: TrainingArguments explicitly allows privacy_noise_mechanism='mf_band' with sampling_mode='poisson' (_training_arguments.py:188 `"mf_band": frozenset({"b_min_sep", "poisson"})`, comment :182 calls it a 'looser-but-valid alternative'), but for that mode build_amplifier_factory constructs the CyclicPoisson horizon accountant (`_ftrl_poisson(mf_gaussian(nm, BandMfStrategy), sample_rate, n_steps)`, _dpftrl.py:140-154) while build_sampler constructs the plain DP-SGD `PoissonSampler` (_dpftrl.py:224-233, imported from opaque.dpsgd.sampling), not the `CyclicPoissonSampler` the accountant's analysis requires. CyclicPoisson.pld_at charges only `num_groups = ceil(n_steps/bands)` compositions of a Poisson-Gaussian at per-participation sensitivity 1 (_poisson.py:179-188, 214), which is the amplified-BandMF reduction (Choquette-Choo et al. 2023, arXiv:2306.08153) valid only when each example can participate in at most one step per bands-wide window (the cyclic group scheme). Plain Poisson samples every example independently at every one of the n steps (dpsgd/_poisson.py:33-38), so a record participates ~Binomial(n, q) times with no separation guarantee — both the composition count (n/bands vs ~n effective) and the per-window sensitivity assumption are violated. Both mid-run epsilon_at (via per_step -> pld_at(K), _dp_trainer.py:1766, 3960) and noise-multiplier calibration (_dp_trainer.py:4222-4237) use this accountant, so the run is calibrated against and reports an epsilon that does not bound the deployed mechanism.
findings.failure_scenario: User sets privacy_noise_mechanism='mf_band' (bands=16 default), sampling_mode='poisson' (passes validation at _training_arguments.py:1048), n=1600 steps, q=0.01, target eps=1. Calibration sizes nm so that ceil(1600/16)=100 Poisson-Gaussian compositions hit eps=1; the deployed run actually gives each record ~16 expected participations across all 1600 steps with possible same-band-window repeats. Measured reference: 100 compositions of poisson(gaussian(1.0), 0.01) give eps(1e-6)=0.954 while the 1600-composition independent-noise reference gives 2.649 — the true epsilon of the deployed banded mechanism under plain Poisson is at least on that order, so the reported/calibrated epsilon is ~2.8x too small at bands=16 and grows with bands. Silent: no warning, training completes, accountant.json records the invalid bound.

findings.title: BallsInBins.pld_at docstring claims K-epoch reparameterization for BSR/BiSR/lambda-CGD and carries an unreachable BLT pinned-prefix gram branch
findings.claim: The pld_at docstring (:150-152) states 'For horizon-independent inners (Identity, BSR, BiSR, lambda-CGD) the gram / primitive is reparameterised by K_epochs' and describes an N-pinned BLT prefix gram (:152-156), but the guard at :181 (`if not isinstance(s, IdentityStrategy) and rounded < self.n_steps: return self.pld_at(self.n_steps, ...)`) snaps EVERY non-Identity prefix to the full-horizon PLD. The BLT pinned-coefficient branch (:216-235) and the BSR/BiSR/lambda-CGD `gram_matrix(n_steps=rounded)` branch (:236-244) therefore only execute with rounded == self.n_steps, where they reproduce the full-horizon gram — the prefix differentiation is dead code, and the docstring contradicts its own last two sentences (:156-158, 'Correlated-strategy Monte Carlo paths use the full-horizon confidence bound for every nonzero prefix'). Behavior is conservative (full-horizon PLD dominates any prefix by post-processing over the causal streaming transcript), so this is a maintenance trap, not a privacy defect.

findings.title: b-min-sep warm-start likelihood ratio misnormalizes the stationary mixture; the #748 confidence bound certifies the wrong functional and the add-direction PLD is anti-conservative
findings.claim: likelihood_ratio_warm computes `sum_f = f[0] + p*tail/denom` (denom = 1+(b-1)p), i.e. it divides only the barred-start terms by the warm-start normalizer while leaving f[0] undivided. The code's own remove-direction sampler `sample_x_under_p` (mc.rs:85-108) draws the initial barred state from the stationary distribution P(state 0)=1/denom, P(state j)=p/denom, whose exact density ratio is (f[0] + p*sum_{j=1}^{b-1} f[j])/denom. The coded expression is therefore not the likelihood ratio of ANY initial-state mixture (its E_Q would need weights summing to 1+(b-1)p/denom > 1). Consequently the Monte Carlo 'privacy loss' samples fed into the PR #748 confidence-band machinery (samples_to_pmf) are ln of an inflated statistic, not the true log-likelihood ratio: the remove-direction PLD is inflated (still an upper bound, but systematically loose by up to ~ln(1+(b-1)p)), and the add-direction PLD is shifted DOWN, so the add-direction epsilon/delta certificate is invalid (underestimates the true add-direction hockey-stick). The final epsilon = max(remove, add); when the deflated add side binds (possible after composing the asymmetric MC PLD with other mechanisms, or in configs where add dominates), the reported 'high-confidence bound' understates the true epsilon. This is reachable from the public API via opaque.dpftrl.accounting.b_min_sep (packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_b_min_sep/__init__.py:191-214 calls _native.bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld / bandmf_b_min_sep_pld_from_transcript_handle), and the July audit's closed issue #337 ('Return conservative privacy guarantees from Monte Carlo amplification', claimed fixed by #748) is therefore incompletely fixed on this path. The runtime BMinSepSampler also uses the stationary warm start (July audit master list line 158 verified P(eligible)=1/(1+(b-1)p)), so the accountant's functional mismatches the deployed mechanism, not just its own internal sampler. The bug predates the audit (introduced in commit 5de05eb0, PR #121) and survived both the audit and PR #748, which rewrote the surrounding sample-to-PMF pipeline without touching these four lines. Distinct from open issue #697 (prefix tightness / MC-error certification): this is a wrong likelihood-ratio functional, not an uncertified error.
findings.failure_scenario: User configures BandMF with b-min-sep sampling, e.g. bands=2, p=0.05, n=50, sigma=1.0 (the repo's own mc_pld_smoke configuration). Faithful Python reimplementation of the Rust code (verified line-by-line against mc.rs:25-76): E_Q[r_code] = 1.16647 +/- 0.003 vs required 1.0 (analytic prediction 1+(b-1)p/denom = 1.16667 at p=0.2); importance-sampling identity P[ln r > t] = E_Q[r*1{ln r>t}] fails for the coded r (0.4597 vs 0.5366 at t=0.5) and holds for the corrected r (0.3939 vs 0.3939). Epsilon impact at delta=0.01 (plain-MC hockey stick, 60k samples): CODE eps_remove=1.286 / eps_add=0.720 vs TRUE eps_remove=1.239 / eps_add=0.766 -- the standalone reported max is inflated ~4% (silent over-noising after calibration), and the add-direction certificate underestimates the true add epsilon by ~6%; with larger bands*p (e.g. bands=32, p=0.02, denom=1.62) the remove inflation grows toward ln(1.62)~0.48 whole-run epsilon while the add deficit grows symmetrically. In any composition where the add adjacency binds the composed maximum, the returned '1-mc_failure_probability confidence' epsilon is below the true epsilon: silent privacy loss.

findings.title: b-min-sep Monte Carlo epsilon depends on Rayon thread count with a fixed seed -- the #331 reproducibility fix covered only balls-in-bins, not the sibling sampler PR #748 also touched
findings.claim: Closed issue #331 ('Make balls-in-bins Monte Carlo reproducible across thread counts') was fixed by giving bnb_mc_pld fixed 1024-sample shards whose seeds depend only on the shard index (monte_carlo.rs:43-55: 'The shard count must depend only on the resolved sample count, not on the Rayon worker count: users expect a fixed seed to select the same samples on every machine'). The sibling MC sampler bandmf_b_min_sep_warm_mc_pld -- rewritten by the same PR #748 for the confidence-bound plumbing -- still partitions its RNG streams by `rayon::current_num_threads()` and seeds per-thread StdRngs as seed+tid (remove) and seed+1000+tid (add), so the drawn sample set, and therefore the reported epsilon, changes with the machine's core count. bandmf_b_min_sep_prepare_transcripts (mc.rs:174-218) has the same dependence even though it runs serially (it deliberately mirrors the thread partition), so cached transcript corpora prepared on one machine differ from another; the Python transcript cache key (packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_b_min_sep/_transcript_cache.py:32 `key = (strategy_coef, n_steps, p, num_mc_samples, mc_seed)`) does not capture the thread count, so identical keys map to different corpora across environments. Reproducibility is a documented contract of `seed` ('RNG seed for Monte Carlo reproducibility', discretization.py:25/123) and the only regression test (tests/test_balls_in_bins_reproducible.py) covers balls-in-bins alone. Additionally, seed+1000+tid collides with the remove streams whenever current_num_threads() > 1000 (remove tid=1000 equals add tid=0), which would reuse identical randomness across adjacency directions on very large machines.

Each individual value is still a valid confidence bound for its own sample set (given finding 1 is fixed), so this is silent nondeterminism of the reported guarantee rather than an invalid bound.

findings.title: Coin flips are positional and invariant to the canary pool, enabling silent audit invalidation under key reuse
findings.claim: The in/out coin mask is a pure function of (key, num_canaries) — `coin_rng = np.random.default_rng(fold_in(key, _COIN_FLIP_DOMAIN).seed); in_mask = coin_rng.random(num_canaries) < 0.5` — so it is byte-identical across every candidate_indices value (pinned as intended behavior by tests/auditing/test_audit.py:467 `np.testing.assert_array_equal(pooled._in_mask, expected_mask)`), prefix-stable across num_canaries, and fully caller-computable before the pool is committed. Coins are then assigned to records positionally through the selection permutation of np.unique(pool). This makes the one-run fair-coin independence assumption unverifiable and easy to violate silently whenever a key is reused across pool iterations, which the docs themselves encourage (every snippet uses key(42)).
findings.failure_scenario: (a) Inflation/false alarm: a caller (or an automated canary-crafting loop) that computes the deterministic record→coin map before training — reproduced in 6 lines from public API — and correlates canary content with the precomputed coin (e.g. places duplicates of always-in rows at coin=in indices and OOD garbage at coin=out indices) gets honest loss_scores that separate perfectly regardless of DP noise. Demonstrated end-to-end: for a mechanism with ZERO leakage (scores set equal to the precomputed coins via public canary_scores), one_run reports eps_delta().epsilon_at(delta=0) = 5.81 and gdp epsilon_at(delta=1e-5) = 38.2 at m=1000 — the audit 'lower bound' exceeds any real guarantee. (b) Silent corruption on drift: editing the pool by ONE element under the same key reassigns in/out for ~half the shared records (measured 45/100 flipped between candidate_indices=range(1000,1100) and range(1000,1101)). A workflow that recreates the partition in a separate eval script (natural, since coin_flip is documented as 'reproducible' from the key) with a pool that drifted by one record silently splits honest scores against membership labels that are ~uncorrelated with the ones used in training — one_run raises nothing and reports a meaningless epsilon in either direction.
evidence: packages/opaque-auditing/src/opaque/api/auditing/_coin_flip.py:353-358: `rng = np.random.default_rng(fold_in(key, _CANARY_SELECTION_DOMAIN).seed); canary_indices = rng.choice(population, size=num_canaries, replace=False); coin_rng = np.random.default_rng(fold_in(key, _COIN_FLIP_DOMAIN).seed); in_mask = np.asarray(coin_rng.random(num_canaries) < _INCLUSION_PROBABILITY, dtype=bool)` — coin stream never sees the pool or the selected identities.

packages/opaque-auditing/tests/auditing/test_audit.py:440-467: test_coin_flip_uses_reproducible_domain_separated_keys asserts `pooled._in_mask == expected_mask` where pooled uses candidate_indices=range(50,100) and expected_mask comes from the un-pooled call — the invariance is test-pinned.

Empirical (run in this session, commit 4b13d82): mask full==poolA True; mask full==poolB True (pool sizes 100 and 101); records whose in/out flipped after adding one pool element: 45 of 100; caller-side coin prediction from fold_in(key,'opaque.auditing.canary_selection')/'opaque.auditing.coin_flip' matches cf.in_indices exactly; coin stream prefix-stable across num_canaries (mask[:100] of m=200 equals mask of m=100).

Empirical inflation demo: cf2 = coin_flip(ds, num_canaries=1000, key=key(42), candidate_indices=range(1000)); scores = 1.0 where index in cf2.in_indices else 0.0; one_run(canary_scores(...), coin_flip=cf2) → eps_delta epsilon_at(delta=0) = 5.809, gdp epsilon_at(delta=1e-5) = 38.25 — with scores that contain no information about any training run.

docs/user-guide/auditing.md (Stronger canaries): 'Fix the pool before target training, independently of that run's membership coins' — an obligation the API makes uncheckable (the coins are a deterministic public function of key and num_canaries, computable before the pool is fixed) and does not detect violations of.

One-run validity requires the membership coins to be uniform and independent of the guessing strategy/canary choice: Steinke, Nasr, Jagielski (2023), arXiv:2305.08846, Theorem 5.2 (coins S_i i.i.d. and independent of everything the adversary controls); the same assumption carries into Xiang et al. (2025), arXiv:2509.08704.

findings.title: Lambda-CGD noise stream is unrooted: fold_in(key, step) collides with the caller's documented key space (missed by fix #728)
findings.claim: Commit 6f6d132a (fix(random)!: namespace mechanism RNG stream roots, #728) established the repo-wide invariant that every mechanism folds a unique string tag into the key it is given before deriving per-step keys ('every stream root Opaque derives for itself is a namespaced string' — noise_allocation.py:25-38; docs/reference/rng.md tag table), and applied it to DP-SGD Gaussian (GAUSSIAN_STREAM_FOLD, _gaussian.py:71), MF dense+streaming (MF_GAUSSIAN_STREAM_FOLD, _engine.py:37,167,395), second-moment, adaptive clipping, and auditing. Lambda-CGD's PRNG-replay noise was missed: _lambda_cgd.py:280 'current_key = rng_fold_in(st._rng_key, step)' and :292 'prev_key = rng_fold_in(st._rng_key, step - 1)' derive privacy-noise generators directly on the caller's integer fold path. Since split(key, n) is defined as fold_in(key, i) (random/_engine.py:127) and the docs explicitly assign integer folds to the caller ('Integers are the caller's... every key split hands back'; rng.md recommends 'noise_key = fold_in(base, step)' and the split loop pattern), any caller that reuses the base key it gave lambda-CGD for an ordinary integer derivation obtains byte-identical torch.Generator streams to the mechanism's privacy noise. The public path is unguarded end to end: mf_gaussian_noise(strategy=lambda_cgd_strategy(...), key=user_key) -> _make_raw_mf_noise (_mf_gaussian_noise.py:131-139, 231-233, no root fold) -> LambdaCgdStrategy.raw_noise_factory (_lambda_cgd.py:152-169) -> fold_in(user_key, step). BiSR, the only other strategy with raw_noise_factory, routes through the rooted _matrix_factorization_noise (_bisr.py:131), so lambda-CGD is the sole surviving instance of the exact defect pattern #728 fixed. The guard test test_stream_root_namespacing.py cannot catch it because it only checks enumerated string constants, and lambda-CGD has none.
findings.failure_scenario: User writes the documented pattern: base = key(42); passes base to mf_gaussian_noise(strategy=lambda_cgd_strategy(...), key=base) and elsewhere derives step_k via split(base) or fold_in(base, step) for their own generator_from_key draws (dropout, data augmentation, a second mechanism, a logged/released random quantity). Reproduced live: with k = key(42), torch.randn(5, generator=generator_from_key(split(k, 2)[0])) is torch.equal to the lambda-CGD step-0 privacy noise (both [0.9301, 0.2699, 0.5048, -1.2086, -0.0477]). If the colliding stream is observable (released values, deterministic replay of user-side randomness), the DP noise is exactly predictable and the effective epsilon is unbounded, with no warning, error, or accounting signal. Restarting a fresh lambda-CGD mechanism with the same key also byte-replays the previous run's noise (correlated releases the fixed-horizon MF accounting does not model).

findings.title: Samplers seed numpy RNG from the raw key with no domain separation (same defect class as #728, sibling surface)
findings.claim: The samplers consume the caller's key without any mechanism root: PoissonSampler does 'self.generator = np.random.default_rng(key.seed)' (_poisson.py:108), balls-in-bins does 'generator = np.random.default_rng(key.seed)' (_balls_in_bins.py:103), and random allocation does 'rng = np.random.default_rng(fold_in(self._key, epoch).seed)' (_random_allocation.py:125) — a bare integer fold on the caller's path. Under the convention #728 shipped ('a mechanism that draws randomness folds one unique string tag into the key it was given', rng.md:208-210), sampling is a randomness-drawing mechanism whose stream should be namespaced: two different samplers built from the same key draw identical PCG64 streams, and random-allocation's epoch stream is byte-identical to any caller-side np.random.default_rng(fold_in(key, epoch).seed). Sampling randomness is amplification-relevant, so stream reuse is not merely a reproducibility nit. Mitigating factors keep this low: the trainer derives the sampler key from data_seed/seed with its own string fold on the restart path (_dp_trainer.py:3688-3703), only one sampler is built per run, and the torch-side noise streams are blake2b-separated from key.seed, so no in-repo default collides.
findings.failure_scenario: A manual-loop user holds one master key and passes it to both a Poisson sampler and a balls-in-bins sampler (e.g. comparing samplers, or train + canary-insertion sampling): both consume np.random.default_rng(key.seed) and draw the identical stream, so the two 'independent' sampling processes are perfectly correlated — participation patterns coincide and any analysis multiplying their probabilities (or treating one as fresh randomness) is wrong. Similarly, a caller that publishes anything derived from default_rng(fold_in(key, epoch).seed) has published the random-allocation assignment stream, voiding the allocation's secrecy assumption. Silent in all cases.
